definitions.explanation: To wake a sleeping person by physically shaking them — typically the shoulder. Implies more vigor than simply calling their name.

examples.japanese: {弟|おとうと}を{揺|ゆ}り{起|お}こした。
examples.english: I shook my little brother awake.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}に{気付|きづ}かない{父|ちち}を{母|はは}が{揺|ゆ}り{起|お}こした。
examples.english: My mother shook my father awake when he didn't notice the earthquake.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{終点|しゅうてん}に{着|つ}いたので、{駅員|えきいん}が{眠|ねむ}っている{乗客|じょうきゃく}を{揺|ゆ}り{起|お}こしている。
examples.english: Since the train has arrived at the last stop, the station staff are shaking the sleeping passengers awake.

notes:
Compound of {揺|ゆ}する (to shake) + {起|お}こす (to wake). Specifically refers to waking by physical shaking, distinguishing it from waking by voice or alarm.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive (takes を). The object is always a person.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肩|かた}を{揺|ゆ}り{起|お}こす: to shake by the shoulder to wake
- {子供|こども}を{揺|ゆ}り{起|お}こす: to shake a child awake
- {寝|ね}ている{人|ひと}を{揺|ゆ}り{起|お}こす: to shake a sleeping person awake

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {起|お}こす: to wake up (someone) — general, by any means
- {揺|ゆ}する: to shake — just the shaking action
- {目覚|めざ}めさせる: to make wake up — broader, includes mental awakening (figurative use too)
